questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In Mulliken notation for irreducible representations, the symbol $B_{2u}$ denotes a representation that is
optionsEn: one-dimensional, symmetric with respect to the principal $C_n$ axis, and antisymmetric with respect to inversion $i$
two-dimensional, antisymmetric with respect to the principal $C_n$ axis, and symmetric with respect to inversion $i$
one-dimensional, antisymmetric with respect to the principal $C_n$ axis, and antisymmetric with respect to inversion $i$
one-dimensional, antisymmetric with respect to the principal $C_n$ axis, and symmetric with respect to inversion $i$
questions.explanationEn: In Mulliken notation: $A$ and $B$ denote 1D representations, where $B$ is antisymmetric ($\chi = -1$) under rotation about the principal $C_n$ axis; the subscript $2$ indicates antisymmetry under a perpendicular $C_2$ or $\sigma_v$; and the subscript $u$ (*ungerade*) indicates antisymmetry ($\chi = -1$) under inversion $i$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a rigid diatomic molecule with rotational constant $B$, the wavenumber of the first rotational Raman Stokes line ($J = 0 \to 2$) shifted from the exciting Rayleigh line is
questions.explanationEn: For pure rotational Raman spectroscopy of a linear rigid rotor, the selection rule is $\Delta J = \pm 2$ and the shift from the Rayleigh line is $|\Delta\tilde{\nu}| = B(4J + 6)$ for $J \to J + 2$. For the first Stokes line ($J = 0 \to 2$), the shift is $B(0 + 6) = 6B$ (while subsequent lines are spaced by $4B$). Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the vibration-rotation infrared spectrum of a diatomic molecule like $\text{HBr}$, the $P$-branch corresponds to the rotational selection rule
questions.explanationEn: In a rovibrational IR band of a closed-shell diatomic molecule ($^1\Sigma$ ground state), the selection rule is $\Delta v = +1, \Delta J = \pm 1$. Transitions with $\Delta J = -1$ (lower frequency than the band origin) form the $P$-branch, while $\Delta J = +1$ (higher frequency) form the $R$-branch; $\Delta J = 0$ ($Q$-branch) is forbidden. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $^{19}\text{F}$ NMR spectrum of $\text{PF}_5$ at room temperature (rapid Berry pseudorotation), the resonance appears as a
questions.explanationEn: At room temperature, rapid Berry pseudorotation renders all five fluorine atoms of $\text{PF}_5$ chemically equivalent on the NMR timescale. Each $^{19}\text{F}$ nucleus couples to the single central $^{31}\text{P}$ nucleus ($I = 1/2$, $100\%$ abundance), splitting the $^{19}\text{F}$ resonance into $2(1)(1/2) + 1 = 2$ lines, i.e., a doublet. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following is an essential condition for sustained laser action (light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation)?
optionsEn: A two-level system pumped solely by continuous optical radiation
Spontaneous emission rate exceeding the stimulated emission rate
Thermal equilibrium obeying the Boltzmann distribution
Population inversion between the upper and lower lasing levels
questions.explanationEn: For net optical gain, the rate of stimulated emission ($B_{21}\rho N_2$) must exceed the rate of stimulated absorption ($B_{12}\rho N_1$). Since $B_{21} = B_{12}$ (for non-degenerate levels), amplification strictly requires population inversion ($N_2 > N_1$), which cannot be achieved in steady state by optical pumping of a 2-level system. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecules are classified as symmetric top (symmetric rotor) molecules?
questions.explanationEn: A symmetric top has two equal principal moments of inertia (distinct from the third), which occurs for any non-linear molecule with a single $C_n$ axis of order $n \ge 3$ (and not belonging to $T_d, O_h, I_h$). Thus $\text{NH}_3$ ($C_{3v}$, oblate), $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$ ($D_{6h}$, oblate), and $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ ($C_{3v}$, prolate) are symmetric tops. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($C_{2v}$) is an asymmetric top ($I_a \neq I_b \neq I_c$). Hence, (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following species are EPR active?
questions.explanationEn: EPR activity requires at least one unpaired electron ($S > 0$). $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ ($3d^1$, D), $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_8^{\bullet -}$ ($S = 1/2$, C), and nitric oxide $\text{NO}$ ($11$ valence electrons, one unpaired in $\pi^*$, A) are all paramagnetic and EPR active. Low-spin $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ ($t_{2g}^6$, $S = 0$, B) is diamagnetic and EPR silent. Hence, (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of normal modes of vibration of a benzene molecule ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For a non-linear polyatomic molecule with $N$ atoms, the number of normal vibrational modes is $3N - 6$. Benzene has $N = 12$ atoms ($6\text{ C} + 6\text{ H}$), giving $3(12) - 6 = 30$ normal modes.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: At low temperature ($-60\,^\circ\text{C}$), where intramolecular exchange is frozen, the number of chemically distinct signals observed in the $^{19}\text{F}$ NMR spectrum of T-shaped $\text{ClF}_3$ is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Chlorine trifluoride ($\text{ClF}_3$) adopts a T-shaped ($C_{2v}$) structure derived from a trigonal bipyramid with two equatorial lone pairs. Consequently, it has two equivalent axial fluorine atoms and one distinct equatorial fluorine atom, giving $2$ signals (a doublet and a triplet in a $2:1$ ratio) at low temperature.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In $^{57}\text{Fe}$ Mössbauer spectroscopy, when a magnetic iron compound experiences internal magnetic hyperfine (Zeeman) splitting, the nuclear transition between $I = \frac{1}{2}$ and $I = \frac{3}{2}$ obeying $\Delta m_I = 0, \pm 1$ splits into _____ allowed lines (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In a magnetic field, the $I = 1/2$ ground state splits into $2$ sublevels ($m_I = \pm 1/2$) and the $I = 3/2$ excited state splits into $4$ sublevels ($m_I = \pm 3/2, \pm 1/2$). Applying the magnetic dipole selection rule $\Delta m_I = 0, \pm 1$ allows exactly $6$ transitions (a characteristic magnetic sextet).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a trigonal planar $\text{AB}_3$ molecule belonging to $D_{3h}$, the irreducible representations of its $4$ normal modes of vibration are $\Gamma_{\text{vib}} = A_1' + A_2'' + 2E'$. Given that $z$ transforms as $A_2''$, $(x, y)$ as $E'$, and quadratic functions as $A_1'$, $E'$, and $E''$, the number of IR-active and Raman-active fundamental bands are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: A vibrational mode is IR active if it transforms as $x, y,$ or $z$ ($A_2''$ and $E'$), and Raman active if it transforms as a quadratic function ($A_1', E', E''$). From $\Gamma_{\text{vib}} = A_1' + A_2'' + 2E'$: IR-active bands are $A_2''$ (1) + $2E'$ (2) $= 3$ bands; Raman-active bands are $A_1'$ (1) + $2E'$ (2) $= 3$ bands (note that the two $E'$ modes are both IR and Raman active). Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a linear rigid rotor with rotational constant $\tilde{B}$ at temperature $T$, the rotational quantum number $J_{\max}$ corresponding to the maximum thermal population (maximum microwave line intensity) is given by the nearest integer to
questions.explanationEn: The thermal population of level $J$ is proportional to $(2J + 1)\exp\left(-\frac{hc\tilde{B}J(J+1)}{k_B T}\right)$. Differentiating with respect to $J$ and setting $\frac{dN_J}{dJ} = 0$ gives $2 - (2J+1)^2\frac{hc\tilde{B}}{k_B T} = 0 \implies 2J + 1 = \sqrt{\frac{2k_B T}{hc\tilde{B}}} \implies J_{\max} = \sqrt{\frac{k_B T}{2hc\tilde{B}}} - \frac{1}{2}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the IR spectrum of $\text{CO}_2$, the asymmetric stretch ($\nu_3 = 2349\text{ cm}^{-1}$, parallel band) and the degenerate bend ($\nu_2 = 667\text{ cm}^{-1}$, perpendicular band) show which rotational branch structures, respectively?
optionsEn: $P$, $Q$, and $R$ branches for $\nu_3$; $P$ and $R$ branches only for $\nu_2$
$P$ and $R$ branches only for $\nu_3$; $P$, $Q$, and $R$ branches for $\nu_2$
$P$ and $R$ branches only for both $\nu_3$ and $\nu_2$
questions.explanationEn: In linear $\text{CO}_2$, the asymmetric stretch $\nu_3$ ($\Sigma_u^+$) is a parallel band (oscillating dipole along the molecular axis, $\Delta l = 0$), so $\Delta J = 0$ is forbidden and only $P$ and $R$ branches appear. The bending mode $\nu_2$ ($\Pi_u$) is a perpendicular band (oscillating dipole perpendicular to the axis, $\Delta l = \pm 1$), which allows $\Delta J = 0, \pm 1$, giving a strong central $Q$-branch along with $P$ and $R$ branches. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a two-spin $^1\text{H}$ AX system with chemical shift separation $\Delta\nu = 240\text{ Hz}$ and coupling constant $J_{AX} = 8\text{ Hz}$ on a $300\text{ MHz}$ spectrometer. If the same sample is recorded on a $600\text{ MHz}$ spectrometer, the values of $\Delta\nu$ and $J_{AX}$ become, respectively,
questions.explanationEn:
Chemical shift separation in Hz scales linearly with the spectrometer operating frequency ($\Delta
u = \Delta\delta \cdot 
u_0$), so doubling $
u_0$ from $300$ to $600	ext{ MHz}$ doubles $\Delta
u$ from $240	ext{ Hz}$ to $480	ext{ Hz}$. By contrast, the scalar spin-spin coupling constant $J$ (in Hz) is an intrinsic molecular property completely independent of the external magnetic field $B_0$, so $J_{AX}$ remains $8	ext{ Hz}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In $^{57}\text{Fe}$ Mössbauer spectroscopy, the nuclear radius of the excited state ($I = 3/2$) is SMALLER than that of the ground state ($I = 1/2$), so $\Delta R / R < 0$. Consequently, increasing the $s$-electron density $|\psi_s(0)|^2$ at the $^{57}\text{Fe}$ nucleus causes the isomer shift ($\delta$) to
questions.explanationEn: The Mössbauer isomer shift is proportional to $\frac{\Delta R}{R}\left[|\psi_s(0)|^2_{\text{absorber}} - |\psi_s(0)|^2_{\text{source}}\right]$. Because $\Delta R / R < 0$ for $^{57}\text{Fe}$, an increase in $s$-electron density at the nucleus (for example, going from high-spin $\text{Fe(II)}$ $3d^6$ to $\text{Fe(III)}$ $3d^5$ due to reduced $3d$ shielding of $3s$ electrons) decreases $\delta$ (shifts it toward more negative velocities). Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about rotational spectroscopy of diatomic molecules are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In a microwave spectrum, the intensity of rotational lines increases monotonically with $J$ for all $J \ge 0$.
Homogeneous isotopic substitution (increasing reduced mass $\mu$) decreases the rotational constant $B$.
The rotational constant $B$ is inversely proportional to the square of the bond length $r$.
Pure rotational Raman spectroscopy can determine the bond length of homonuclear diatomics like $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$.
questions.explanationEn: Since $B = \frac{h}{8\pi^2 I c} = \frac{h}{8\pi^2 \mu r^2 c}$, increasing $\mu$ lowers $B$ (B) and $B \propto r^{-2}$ (C). Homonuclear diatomics like $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ have anisotropic polarizability and are rotationally Raman active, enabling bond-length determination (D). Statement (A) is false because line intensities rise to a maximum at $J_{\max}$ and then decay exponentially at higher $J$. Hence, (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about EPR (ESR) spectroscopy are CORRECT?
optionsEn: According to the McConnell relation $a_{\text{H}} = Q \rho_{\text{C}}$, the proton hyperfine coupling constant is proportional to the unpaired $\pi$-spin density $\rho_{\text{C}}$ on the adjacent aromatic carbon.
A free electron has a Landé $g$-factor of exactly $1.0000$.
The selection rules for isotropic EPR transitions with one coupled nucleus are $\Delta M_S = \pm 1$ and $\Delta M_I = 0$.
EPR spectra are conventionally recorded as the first derivative of absorption ($dA/dB$) versus magnetic field $B$ using field modulation.
questions.explanationEn: Standard EPR transitions obey $\Delta M_S = \pm 1, \Delta M_I = 0$ (C), are detected via phase-sensitive lock-in amplification as first-derivative curves $dA/dB$ (D), and for $\pi$-radicals obey McConnell's relation $a_{\text{H}} = Q\rho_{\text{C}}$ with $|Q| \approx 2.3\text{ mT}$ (A). Statement (B) is false because the free-electron $g$-factor is $g_e = 2.0023$. Hence, (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The rotational constant of $^{12}\text{C}^{16}\text{O}$ is $\tilde{B} = 1.931\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The equilibrium bond length of $\text{CO}$ (in $\text{\AA}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _____. (Given: atomic masses $^{12}\text{C} = 12.0\text{ amu}$, $^{16}\text{O} = 16.0\text{ amu}$; $1\text{ amu} = 1.6605 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$; $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$; $c = 2.998 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: Convert $\tilde{B} = 1.931\text{ cm}^{-1} = 193.1\text{ m}^{-1}$. The reduced mass is $\mu = \frac{12 \times 16}{28} \times 1.6605 \times 10^{-27} = 1.1386 \times 10^{-26}\text{ kg}$. From $\tilde{B} = \frac{h}{8\pi^2 I c}$, $I = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{8\pi^2(2.998 \times 10^8)(193.1)} = 1.4496 \times 10^{-46}\text{ kg m}^2$. Hence, $r = \sqrt{I/\mu} = \sqrt{1.2731 \times 10^{-20}} = 1.128 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \approx 1.13\text{ \AA}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An organic free radical with $g = 2.0023$ is examined in an X-band EPR spectrometer operating at a microwave frequency of $9.500\text{ GHz}$. The resonance magnetic field $B_0$ (in $\text{mT}$, rounded off to one decimal place) is _____. (Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $\mu_B = 9.274 \times 10^{-24}\text{ J T}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: From the EPR resonance condition $h\nu = g\mu_B B_0$, we solve $B_0 = \frac{h\nu}{g\mu_B} = \frac{(6.626 \times 10^{-34})(9.500 \times 10^9)}{(2.0023)(9.274 \times 10^{-24})} = 0.33898\text{ T} = 339.0\text{ mT}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a vibrational Raman mode at $\tilde{\nu} = 208.5\text{ cm}^{-1}$ at $300\text{ K}$, the Boltzmann population ratio $\frac{N(v=1)}{N(v=0)}$ governing the anti-Stokes to Stokes intensity ratio (neglecting the $\nu^4$ scattering factor, rounded off to two decimal places) is _____. (Given: $k_B/(hc) = 0.695\text{ cm}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: The thermal population ratio between $v = 1$ and $v = 0$ is $\frac{N_1}{N_0} = \exp\left(-\frac{hc\tilde{\nu}}{k_B T}\right)$. Here $\frac{k_B T}{hc} = 0.695 \times 300 = 208.5\text{ cm}^{-1}$, so $\frac{hc\tilde{\nu}}{k_B T} = \frac{208.5}{208.5} = 1.000$. Thus, $\frac{N_1}{N_0} = e^{-1} = 0.3679 \approx 0.37$.
